newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada board gets Palliser gas line application.
newsitem.headline: Canada board gets Palliser gas line application.

text.p: Canada's National Energy Board said on Wednesday it received Palliser Pipeline Inc 's application to build a 700 km natural gas pipeline to Saskatchewan from Alberta.
The line, which is at the heart of a battle in Alberta over competition in what has been a monopoly for NOVA Corp, would ship 1.2 billion cubic feet of gas per day by November 1998.
Palliser is co-owned by PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd and Westcoast Energy Inc.
The Palliser line, which would extend to southwestern Saskatchewan from north of Calgary, carries an estimated capital cost of C$365 million.
PanCanadian has said it devised the project because much of its gas production lies along the southern Alberta route.
Currently, under a decades-old toll structure called the "postage stamp" rate, it pays the same to ship gas to the border on the NOVA system as shippers in the northernmost regions of the province.

In southwestern Saskatchewan, the Palliser line would interconnect with other pipelines that extend to markets in the U.S. Midwest and Northeast and eastern Canada. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
